title: Zombie Reader/Writer Failures in Redundant Servers
pattern: Activating a replacement server during a rolling migration or failover without immediately deactivating or fencing the old "zombie" server's write permissions.
why_bad: The zombie server can continue to serve stale reads or accept write requests that conflict with writes accepted by the new server, causing silent, permanent data corruption and lost updates [701].
detection: The absence of a fencing token, lease de-registration, or node shutdown call in a server rollover or migration script.
counterexample: Valid if the servers are strictly stateless and write to a single centralized database that handles conflict resolution internally.
fix: Implement a fencing token pattern, use distributed leases with short TTLs, or physically disable the old node's network credentials before activating the replacement [679, 701].
source: A Philosophy of Software Design, "RAMCloud Zombie Servers" [701]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 8 [679]
